title: Standard Demo Deck v1 — Slide-by-slide Guide (Intent, Personas, Required Assets)
author: Soojin Lee
content:
## Purpose
This page is the canonical internal reference for **Standard Demo Deck v1**. It explains, slide-by-slide:
- What each slide is trying to prove
- Which **persona(s)** it is for (Platform Eng, ML Eng, Security/Compliance, Procurement)
- Which screenshots/assets are **required** (and how to keep them current)
- What can be **said safely** vs what must remain ranges / "directionally" true

This deck is designed to pair with the **Standard Demo Tenant** and the master talk track. It is intentionally opinionated: the goal is a repeatable, low-flake narrative that demonstrates Redwood’s differentiators in under 20 minutes, with optional branches.

---

## Where to find the deck
- Source of truth (working file): Google Drive → Go-to-market → “Deck - Redwood Standard Demo (Working)”
- This Confluence page: narrative intent + asset checklist + persona targets

**Change control:** Treat the deck and demo tenant as a coupled system. If you change screenshots, model names, routing policy names, or dashboard panels, validate against the regression checklist (see Demo Tenant Runbook).

---

## Default runtime + timing
**Default runtime (recommended): 18–22 minutes**
- 2–3 min: framing / why Redwood
- 10–12 min: live product proof (Console + one or two API calls)
- 3–5 min: deployment modes + security posture
- 2 min: next steps

**Minimum viable (2–5 min) variant:** Slides 1–4 + one proof slide (typically cost/latency dashboard) + next steps.

---

## Persona routing (which branch to run first)
Use this as a “choose-your-own-adventure” start point:
- **Platform Eng / Infra:** start with reliability + routing/fallback + observability (Slides 6–10)
- **ML Eng / Applied AI:** start with model onboarding + eval/rollouts + structured output/tool calling (Slides 5–9)
- **Security/Compliance:** move Security slide earlier (Slide 13) and keep data handling crisp
- **Procurement / leadership:** keep the technical proof short; emphasize deployment flexibility + operational cost controls; avoid pricing specifics

---

## Screenshot + asset standards (do not skip)
**Why:** Most live-demo failures are avoidable if the deck’s screenshots match the tenant’s current UI and saved views.

**Standards**
- Use the demo tenant only (no customer names, no real prompts from prospects).
- Keep screenshots **crop-tight** around the UI element being discussed.
- Blur/redact any internal-only IDs, emails, or access tokens.
- Use “safe claims”: do not embed absolute latency/cost numbers unless approved in the benchmark proof points table.

**Required screenshot set for v1** (must exist before publishing deck updates)
1) Redwood Console → Routes list (showing a demo route and fallback policy)
2) Redwood Console → Route detail (policy section visible: routing, fallback, quotas)
3) Redwood Console → Rollouts (canary/A-B toggle visible)
4) Redwood Console → Observability dashboard (latency + token cost panels)
5) Redwood Console → Error analysis / traces (one example failure mode + fallback outcome)
6) Deployment modes diagram (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — Redwood-approved visual
7) Security posture slide elements: encryption, retention defaults, RBAC/SSO hooks (no overstated cert claims)

**Owner for screenshots:** Product Marketing (Soojin Lee) with validation from Solutions Engineering (Markus Klein) and Console team (Chloe Martin).

---

## Slide-by-slide guide (Standard Demo Deck v1)

### Slide 1 — Title: “Redwood Inference — Standard Demo”
**Intent:** Set expectations: this is a production inference demo (latency, cost, reliability), not a model capability show.

**Primary persona:** All

**Required asset:** Title slide only (no screenshots)

**Notes:** Keep it neutral and confident. Avoid naming specific competitor providers.

---

### Slide 2 — Agenda: “What we’ll show”
**Intent:** Pre-wire the differentiators and reduce random detours.

**Primary persona:** Procurement/leadership + Platform Eng

**What it must include (bullets):**
- One API interaction (streaming or structured)
- Console proof (latency/cost)
- Reliability (fallback) + operational controls
- Deployment modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)

**Required asset:** Agenda slide

---

### Slide 3 — The problem: “Serving is the bottleneck”
**Intent:** Frame the market thesis: advantage is in serving—latency, unit economics, reliability, deployment flexibility.

**Primary persona:** All (especially leadership)

**Required asset:** Simple diagram or bullets (no benchmarks unless pre-approved)

**Safe language:**
- “We help teams make inference predictable and economical across changing models/hardware.”
- Avoid “X% cheaper” unless explicitly sourced and approved.

---

### Slide 4 — Redwood overview: platform surface area
**Intent:** Establish credibility and mental model: API + Dedicated + Private + Console + Optimize.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng, ML Eng

**Required asset:** Product surface area diagram

**Notes:** Keep it high-level; do not deep dive into kernel details unless asked.

---

### Slide 5 — Demo environment: “What you are seeing”
**Intent:** Increase trust in the demo: stable tenant, pinned versions, repeatable scenarios.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng, Security

**Required screenshot/asset:**
- One screenshot of the demo tenant landing context or a neutral “demo tenant” callout slide

**Must say (briefly):**
- “This demo runs on a dedicated, sanitized demo tenant with pinned model versions and known-good scripts.”

---

### Slide 6 — Scenario 1: “Developer-first API (streaming / structured output)”
**Intent:** Show time-to-value and production features (streaming, structured output, tool calling).

**Primary persona:** ML Eng, Dev-focused champions

**Required assets:**
- Code snippet slide (curl/SDK) using demo-safe prompt
- (Optional) Screenshot of streamed response

**Live demo option:** Run one request (streaming chat OR structured JSON response). Keep it short.

**Fallback if live fails:** Use a prerecorded response snippet (never improvise a new prompt live).

---

### Slide 7 — Proof: “Latency & cost visibility (token-level)”
**Intent:** Show what differentiates Redwood: transparent unit economics and performance breakdown.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng, leadership

**Required screenshot:**
- Observability dashboard: latency percentile panel + token cost breakdown panel

**Safe language:**
- Use relative framing: “Here’s where time and tokens are going” rather than absolute promises.
- If asked for numbers: refer to “Benchmark Proof Points” ranges and customer-specific testing.

---

### Slide 8 — Controls: “Batching, caching, and routing policies”
**Intent:** Demonstrate that cost/performance is controllable with explicit levers.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng

**Required screenshot:**
- Route detail showing policy controls (batching/caching toggles or configuration summary)

**Must show:**
- Where the control lives in the Console
- That changes are observable in metrics

---

### Slide 9 — Reliability: “Fallback routing / graceful degradation”
**Intent:** Prove resilience: keep apps online through model/region/capacity issues.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng, SRE-minded buyers

**Required screenshots:**
- Route list or route detail showing **fallback policy**
- Error analysis panel showing a failure + successful fallback (or simulation)

**Live demo option:** Trigger a controlled failure mode (e.g., route to a constrained capacity tier) and show automatic fallback.

**Safety note:** Only use pre-configured failure toggles from the demo runbook. Do not modify production-like routing rules ad hoc during a call.

---

### Slide 10 — Operations: “Dashboards, alerts, and troubleshooting”
**Intent:** Show readiness for production operations.

**Primary persona:** Platform Eng, Security (audit expectations), leadership

**Required screenshots:**
- “Demo Tenant — Latency/5xx/Throttles” saved view
- (Optional) tracing/error drill-down

**Callouts:**
- “Per-route dashboards”
- “Error budget mindset”
- “Fast triage via traces and error breakdown”

---

### Slide 11 — Rollouts: “Canary / A-B / version pinning”
**Intent:** Show safe iteration: model updates without breaking product behavior.

**Primary persona:** ML Eng + Platform Eng

**Required screenshot:**
- Rollouts UI showing canary or A/B configuration

**Must say:**
- “We pin model versions for repeatability and use controlled rollouts for changes.”

---

### Slide 12 — Deployment modes: Hosted → Dedicated → Private
**Intent:** De-risk enterprise adoption: multiple deployment modes with a consistent interface.

**Primary persona:** Security, Platform Eng, Procurement

**Required asset:**
- Deployment modes diagram (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with one-liner value props

**Notes:** Emphasize “same API + same operational tooling” across modes.

---

### Slide 13 — Security posture (demo-safe)
**Intent:** Provide credible, non-overstated answers to common security questions and redirect to the Security FAQ.

**Primary persona:** Security/Compliance

**Required asset:** Security slide with bullets (no speculative roadmap)

**Must include (approved statements only):**
- Data handling at a high level (no customer data in demo tenant)
- Encryption in transit/at rest (describe generally; avoid implementation claims you can’t prove on the call)
- Access controls: RBAC/SSO integration options (state as “supported” where true; otherwise “available in enterprise plans”)
- Logging/retention posture at a policy level (point to FAQ)

**Do not include:**
- Specific audit report details on a slide (share under separate process)

---

### Slide 14 — Commercial + evaluation path (no pricing numbers)
**Intent:** Make it easy to move forward without getting stuck on list price.

**Primary persona:** Procurement + leadership

**Required asset:**
- Packaging overview (Hosted usage-based, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private licensing) without numbers

**Talk track:**
- “We’ll size based on your workload characteristics and SLOs; we can run a short benchmark/eval to ground this.”

---

### Slide 15 — Next steps: “From demo → eval”
**Intent:** Close with a crisp plan.

**Primary persona:** All

**Required asset:** Next steps slide

**Recommended CTA options:**
- “Sandbox trial on Hosted”
- “Dedicated sizing session”
- “Private/VPC architecture + security review”

---

### Appendix A — Optional deep dive: Architecture overview
**Intent:** Use only if asked; avoid expanding scope.

**Persona:** Platform Eng

**Asset:** Architecture diagram (runtime + orchestration + routing)

---

### Appendix B — Optional: Benchmark methodology / proof points (approved ranges only)
**Intent:** Provide controlled language for performance claims.

**Persona:** Platform Eng + leadership

**Asset:** Only include if validated by PMM/Marketing alignment. Reference “Benchmark Proof Points” source.

---

## “What we show live” vs “what we claim” (guardrails)
**Show live (preferred):**
- One API request (streaming or structured)
- One Console dashboard view (latency + cost)
- One reliability moment (fallback policy visible; optional controlled failure)

**Claim (with evidence links):**
- Deployment modes and operational tooling
- Security posture at a policy level

**Never claim without verification on the call:**
- Hard latency guarantees for a prospect’s workload
- Exact cost per 1M tokens
- Specific compliance certifications unless you are using approved language and can route to the correct process

---

## Versioning policy for this deck (v1)
- This “v1” deck is tied to the **known-good scenario set** and pinned model versions in the demo tenant.
- Any of the following require a **deck review + dry run** before publishing updates:
  - Changing model version(s) or quantization profile(s)
  - Changing route/fallback policy names
  - Console UI changes that move menu items / saved views
  - Changing any screenshots on Slides 7–11 or the security posture slide

**Owner:** Soojin Lee (PMM) for deck; Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) for live-demo feasibility; Chloe Martin (Console) for UI verification.

---

## Quick QA checklist (before marking a deck update “ready”)
1) All required screenshots updated and match current Console UI
2) Demo tenant dashboards load in <10 seconds and panels render correctly
3) One complete run-through completed (driver + narrator), including Plan B
4) Security slide reviewed against current Security FAQ language
5) No pricing numbers or unapproved benchmarks introduced

---

## Support / requests
- For deck edits: file a request with Product Marketing (Soojin Lee)
- For demo tenant issues during prep: follow Demo Tenant Runbook → escalation path (SE → SRE business-hours oncall)
- For security questions: route to Security FAQ and Naomi Feldman / Marcus Lin for approved responses
